name: Scanner_Tool_Implementation
description: The core handheld scanner tool: equip, aim, scan, read-out. Real-time geological/mineral/atmospheric data collection with educational contextual feedback.

questions.question: Does the scanner teach real geological identification through in-game analysis?
questions.answer: Yes. Scanner classifies rock types by grain size, color, hardness, and effervescence. Player learns to identify basalt vs. granite vs. sandstone by observable properties, not just labels.

questions.question: Does the scanner generate screenshot-worthy 'discovery' moments?
questions.answer: Yes. Full scan readout with cross-sectional terrain analysis and annotated mineral layers makes a visually impressive screenshot. Rich HUD overlay with real data is shareable.

questions.question: Does the scanner give meaningful data that changes by location and time?
questions.answer: Yes. Scans differ by biome, altitude, time of day, and weather. Mineral composition, atmosphere, POIs, and hazard warnings all vary dynamically. World feels alive and scientific.

questions.question: Can the scanner be prototyped in one sprint using existing patterns?
questions.answer: Yes. Scanner equips to tool slot using existing Verb_Look/tool-switching patterns. UMG readout display uses standard widgets. Core scan raycast + mineral ID can be built in 3-5 days.

questions.question: Is scanner logic data-driven and extendable?
questions.answer: Yes. Mineral definitions, atmosphere tables, hardness values, and scan range are DataTable-driven. Adding new minerals or gases requires only data changes.

questions.question: Does the scanner work in UE5.8 without hacks?
questions.answer: Yes. Uses GAS (Gameplay Ability System), UMG widgets, line traces -- all standard UE5.8 subsystems. No engine modifications needed.

questions.question: Does the scanner run at 30+ fps on RTX 3060?
questions.answer: Yes. Scanner uses a single line trace on activation (negligible CPU cost), simple data lookup, and lightweight UMG overlay. No GPU impact.

questions.question: Can a colorblind or hearing-impaired player fully use the scanner?
questions.answer: Yes. Results are primarily text-based with icons. Mineral ID uses shape + text, not color-only. Audio scan sound is supplementary.

questions.question: Does the scanner have distinctive sound design?
questions.answer: v1: equip hum, charge-up ascending tone, data-burst release, result ping -- all achievable with synthetic audio. No dedicated audio team needed for prototype.

questions.question: Does the scanner work in multiplayer?
questions.answer: v1 is single-player. Each player has own scanner; scan results are independent. Scan data sharing is v2.

questions.question: Can the community add new scannable items?
questions.answer: Yes. Mineral and atmosphere data tables are JSON/DataTable. Modders add new scannables, data categories, and custom scan feedback.

questions.question: Can scanner data be localized?
questions.answer: Yes. All mineral names, descriptions, property labels, and measurement units use UE5 FText. Scientific symbols and numbers are locale-friendly.

questions.question: Does Scanner_Tool_Implementation depend on Tool_Systems parent?
questions.answer: Yes. Tool_Systems provides the tool-equip framework, slot system, and tool-switching input. Scanner is one tool type within that system.

questions.question: Does Scanner_Tool_Implementation prove educational tools are viable in UE5?
questions.answer: Yes. A working scanner with real scientific data output proves educational content can be delivered through gameplay tools, not menus or text boxes.

questions.question: Was Scanner_Tool_Implementation derived from Tool_Systems Q1 (educational science)?
questions.answer: Yes. Tool_Systems Q1 asked 'Do tools teach real science through their use?' and answered yes. This sub-feature materializes that answer as a specific tool.

questions.question: Does scanner conflict with the environmental demo focus?
questions.answer: No. Scanner enhances the environmental demo. A canyon scan revealing strata layers is a highlight moment that showcases both the environment AND the educational tool.

questions.question: What UE5 knowledge is required for scanner implementation?
questions.answer: GAS, line traces, UMG widgets, data tables. Moderate difficulty. Core scanning logic is ~1 week for a UE5-capable C++ developer.

questions.question: Does this need sub-features or is it detailed enough?
questions.answer: Detailed enough at this level. Future sub-features: Scanner_Mineral_Database, Scanner_Atmosphere_Analyzer, Scanner_Discovery_Log.

questions.question: Are siblings missing at this level?
questions.answer: No. Scanner (core tool), Durability (lifecycle), Crafting (creation) form the complete tool system triad.

questions.question: Is Tool_Systems complete enough to support this?
questions.answer: Yes. Tool_Systems is at DESIGNED status with all 41 questions answered.

questions.question: Should Scanner_Tool_Implementation be built before its siblings?
questions.answer: Yes. Scanner is the highest-priority tool as it directly supports the educational mission and environmental demo.

questions.question: Does Scanner_Tool_Implementation block other features?
questions.answer: Partially. Tool_Crafting_System benefits from scanner (identifying materials) but does not require it. Tool_Durability is independent.

questions.question: Does Scanner_Tool_Implementation serve the educational RPG goal?
questions.answer: Yes. Scanner is the primary educational tool. Through scanning, players learn real geology, meteorology, and astronomy.

questions.question: What is sacrificed by building scanner now?
questions.answer: Building scanner prioritizes educational tool depth over other tool types (weapon, construction). Acceptable: scanner is the most educational tool.

questions.question: What evidence shows real-data scanners drive engagement?
questions.answer: Elite Dangerous' discovery scanner and No Man's Sky's analysis visor prove scan-based gameplay with real data is deeply engaging.

questions.question: Does scanner chain reach a human learning something real?
questions.answer: Yes. Player learns geological identification, Mohs hardness scale, atmospheric science -- transferable scientific literacy skills.

questions.question: Can this feature be verified by sleepwalker beat tests?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can walk through this feature and verify state changes.

questions.question: Does this feature have automated regression tests?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.

questions.question: What are the edge cases and failure modes?
questions.answer: Edge cases include: network interruption, empty state, concurrent access, corrupted data. Documented in threat model.

questions.question: Can this feature be tested in isolation (unit test)?
questions.answer: Partially. Python modules have unit tests. UE5 Blueprint/C++ needs automated test framework.

questions.question: Is there a visual/performance baseline for regression detection?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.

questions.question: Can the Foundry build this feature autonomously via MCP?
questions.answer: Foundry supports this feature via MCP builder. 23 tools available. No new infrastructure needed.

questions.question: Does the Foundry have all needed MCP pathways for this feature?
questions.answer: Foundry supports this feature via MCP builder. 23 tools available. No new infrastructure needed.

questions.question: Does the Foundry need new tools or extensions to support this?
questions.answer: No new MCP tools needed. Existing 23 tools cover all current feature types.

questions.question: Can the Foundry verify this feature via MCP inspect/screenshot?
questions.answer: Yes. MCP inspect confirms actor existence. Screenshot captures visual state.

questions.question: Does the Foundry pipeline handle this feature type (Python/UE5/Blueprints)?
questions.answer: Python features build directly. UE5 features construct via MCP. Blueprint features need manual editor setup.

questions.question: How does scanner hardware tiering (basic vs. advanced vs. professional) create a differentiated tool economy where range, accuracy, and capability correlate with acquisition cost and unlock different economic activities?
questions.answer: Scanner tiers gatekeep economic specialization. A basic scanner (50m range, mineral-only) enables subsistence prospecting. A professional scanner (500m, full spectral/biological/atmospheric) unlocks deep vein location, rare-organism identification, and quality prediction. Premium scanners are capital investments that pay off only with volume — shaping career choice.

questions.question: Does the scanner tool itself tell a believable science-fiction story — a handheld device with realistic spectroscopic, LIDAR, and ground-penetrating capabilities that a real field geologist would recognize?
questions.answer: The scanner feels real because its capabilities are real: Raman spectroscopy for minerals, LIDAR for topography, ground-penetrating radar for subsurface structures — tools a field scientist would actually use, adapted for gameplay.

questions.question: Does the equip-aim-scan-read-out flow feel tactile and responsive, with clear visual feedback at each step -- equip animation, targeting reticle, scan progress ring, result card slide-in?
questions.answer: Equip: 0.4s weapon-raise animation with audio click. Aim: reticle tightens from circle to crosshair over 0.2s. Scan: progress ring fills clockwise (0.5-1.5s). Result: card slides in from bottom edge over 0.3s. Each step has distinct sound + visual.

questions.question: Does the scanner's active state, current mode selection, and target lock need to persist between sessions?
questions.answer: Partially. Active state (equipped/not) is transient. Mode selection (geology vs atmosphere vs biology) should persist once unlocked. Target lock is transient. Written on mode change (infrequent).

questions.question: What physical principles govern the scanner's interaction with materials: does it use simulated reflectivity, density, or composition data, or a lookup table?
questions.answer: Lookup table driven by the graph knowledge base. When the scanner targets a canyon wall, it queries the feature graph for the geological data at that location. No simulated physics interaction with the material itself.
